questions.question: Which language should the React Native mobile client use?
questions.rationale: React Native is the settled client framework, and TypeScript fits the shared API/data-model architecture in the README.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Recommended for shared models and safer API integration.

questions.question: Which mobile framework should the client use?
questions.rationale: The user and repository README identify React Native as the client framework.

options.label: React Native
options.description: Settled default for a shared architecture and native mobile experience.

questions.question: For the first read-only dashboard, what account information and account-linking behavior should the mobile client support? Please specify whether the first test should use a mock provider, a real Kalshi connection, or both.
questions.answer: Connect a real Kalshi account and show synced account balance, positions, and market data. The dashboard is read-only; order placement is out of scope.
questions.rationale: The README permits mock or real provider linking but does not settle the initial test mode or which unified account fields to display.

questions.question: Which language should the Node.js backend use?
questions.rationale: Node.js is settled; TypeScript is a practical default for the provider-neutral API and shared models.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Recommended for provider and API contracts shared with the mobile client.

questions.question: Which Node.js framework should the provider-neutral API use?
questions.rationale: The user settled Node.js and Azure App Service but left Express versus NestJS open.

options.label: Express
options.description: Lightweight, straightforward framework for a small initial API.

options.label: NestJS
options.description: More structured framework with conventions suited to a growing provider integration layer.

questions.question: Are there any additional first-milestone API or provider-integration requirements beyond read-only account linking, a provider-neutral design, and Kalshi as the first provider?
questions.answer: Use a provider-neutral API hosted on Azure App Service, Azure SQL persistence, Microsoft Entra External ID for user authentication, and Azure Key Vault for server-side Kalshi credentials. Do not place or modify orders, and do not provision Azure resources during scaffolding.
questions.rationale: The repository establishes the initial goal, but does not specify operational or integration details such as refresh behavior or mock-provider expectations.

questions.question: Which datastore should persist application and linked-account data?
questions.rationale: The user has not selected between PostgreSQL and Azure SQL; persistence is expected for linked account data.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Recommended relational datastore for account and provider-normalized records.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only if the initial application does not persist data.

questions.question: Should users sign in to use the application's account and API features?
questions.rationale: The user confirmed that sign-in is required and selected Microsoft Entra External ID.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require user sign-in for account linking and application API features.
